cases.case: Jaya Thakur v. Union of India (challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023)
cases.issue: Whether Sections 6 and 7 of the 2023 Act, which removed the Chief Justice of India from the panel that selects the CEC and Election Commissioners, compromise the Election Commission's independence.
cases.bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and S.C. Sharma (CJI Surya Kant recused on 20 Mar 2026)
cases.status_text: Referred to a Constitution Bench
cases.last_event: The two judges split on whether a larger bench was needed, then unanimously sent the papers to the CJI so a Constitution Bench can be constituted. Decision had been reserved on 30 Jul 2026.
cases.next_step: Constitution Bench to be constituted; no hearing date announced. Separately, on 5 Oct 2026 a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the ECI on a plea asking whether CEC Gyanesh Kumar can individually exercise powers vested in the full Commission, and said 'Any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us' (IANS; PTI). On 27 Oct 2026 the same bench heard Rakesh Kumar Singh v. Union of India (W.P.(C) No. 1246/2026) and connected pleas alleging the CEC took SIR decisions without the concurrence of Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, gave the petitioners two weeks to file a rejoinder to the Commission's counter-affidavit, passed no interim order and listed the matter for 17 Nov 2026 (LawChakra).

cases.case: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh
cases.issue: Whether to revisit the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply test for what counts as an 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act.
cases.bench: Nine judges led by CJI Surya Kant
cases.status_text: Decided, split verdict
cases.last_event: Four judges backed the CJI's narrower 'discernible commercial character' test; four (Nagarathna, Datta, Bhuyan, Bagchi) backed the 1978 test; Justice P.S. Narasimha left the 1978 test undisturbed because the ID Act has been repealed. The 1978 test continues for pending ID Act disputes.
cases.next_step: None in this case. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 definition is to be read on its own terms.

cases.case: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India and connected SIR petitions
cases.issue: Legality of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar and later phases.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi (Bihar ruling)
cases.status_text: Bihar SIR upheld; later-phase challenges pending
cases.last_event: On 4 Nov 2026 Prashant Bhushan, for Delhi petitioners Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, mentioned before CJI Surya Kant that the ECI's 3 Nov clarification (that electors left out of the draft roll may file Form 6, with no action under Section 31 of the RP Act, 1950, on that ground alone) runs against the Court's 28 Oct observation that such voters cannot be compelled to use Form 6 and should be allowed Form 8 or the enumeration form. The CJI said people 'need not be apprehensive', asked for an application and indicated the Court could ask the ECI to extend the deadline. About 47.56 lakh Delhi electors were left out of the draft roll. Earlier: notice on a Delhi petition in September; ECI told in August to disclose pending West Bengal appeals; Bihar SIR upheld unanimously on 27 May 2026.
cases.next_step: Delhi Form 6 issue to be heard on 19 Nov 2026; West Bengal matters pending. Separately, on 6 Nov 2026 the ECI gave electors marked absent, shifted, dead or duplicate in the SIR draft rolls of Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland a fresh chance to file enumeration forms (online on ECINET or to BLOs and EROs) before the final rolls; no deadline was given.

cases.case: Jagtar Singh Hawara's plea for transfer from Tihar Jail, Delhi, to a prison in Punjab
cases.issue: Whether Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, should be moved to a Punjab jail, mainly so he can meet his elderly mother.
cases.bench: Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale
cases.status_text: Deferred until after the Punjab Assembly elections
cases.last_event: Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati cited an Intelligence Bureau report, sought by the court after the Punjab government raised law-and-order concerns, which said a transfer would have a 'huge impact' on the upcoming state elections and placed Hawara in the high-risk category. Justice Sundresh called the report 'very damning'. The Home Ministry said Tihar is more secure for high-security prisoners. Senior Advocate S Muralidhar, for Hawara, said a parole plea is pending in the Punjab and Haryana High Court and suggested the matter be taken up after the elections; the court agreed.
cases.next_step: Hearing after the Punjab Assembly elections, due early 2027: PTI says February 2027; LiveLaw says three months after the elections.

cases.case: Goa government's planned Special Leave Petition against the Bombay High Court (Goa bench) interim stay on notifying Goa's ST population estimates (challenge to the Readjustment of Representation of Scheduled Tribes in Assembly Constituencies of the State of Goa Act, 2025)
cases.issue: Whether the Census Commissioner can notify an estimated Scheduled Tribe population for Goa, a step needed to reserve assembly seats for STs before the 2027 election.
cases.bench: High Court: Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit S. Jamsandekar; Supreme Court bench not yet assigned
cases.status_text: SLP against High Court stay announced; filing not confirmed
cases.last_event: Goa NRI Commissioner Narendra Sawaikar said the state would seek to vacate the High Court stay and file a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court by Wednesday. A delegation met Solicitor General Tushar Mehta in New Delhi on 2 Nov; the Centre and the ST community also plan to approach the Court. The High Court's interim order of 29 Oct 2026 in Edwin Lucio Fernandes v. Union of India (Writ Petition No. 1415 of 2026), which restrained the Census Commissioner from notifying the estimated ST figures pending the petition, questioned the Census Commissioner's presumption that STs are 9.9% of Goa's population, based on the 2001 Census, noting the Kunbi, Gauda and Velip communities were added to the ST list in January 2003. The order has put the proposed reservation of four assembly constituencies in doubt.
cases.next_step: Filing of the SLP, expected by 4 Nov 2026.

cases.case: Mangala Bhimrao Ingle v. State of Maharashtra (SLP(C) No. 30772/2025), reconsideration of Javed v. State of Haryana (2003)
cases.issue: Whether laws that disqualify people with more than two children from panchayat posts remain valid, and whether the three-judge ruling in Javed v. State of Haryana (2003), which upheld such a bar, should be reconsidered.
cases.bench: Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe
cases.status_text: Javed ruling referred to a larger bench
cases.last_event: The bench said laws penalising having more than two children 'have lost their relevance', noting that India's total fertility rate has fallen to 1.9, below the replacement rate of 2.1, from 3 when Javed was decided. As a two-judge bench cannot overrule a three-judge ruling, it stayed the proceedings and referred Javed to a larger bench. The petitioner, a former sarpanch of Kakoda gram panchayat in Maharashtra, was disqualified under Section 14(1)(j-1) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act, 1959, after her third child; the Court had stayed the High Court order in November 2025 and reserved judgment on 4 Aug 2026.
cases.next_step: Larger bench to be constituted by the CJI; no date set. The two-child norm stays in force in the states that have it until then.

cases.case: Appeals by four accused against the Tripura High Court's refusal of bail in an NDPS Act case (case title not reported)
cases.issue: Whether the 24-hour limit under Article 22(2) of the Constitution to produce an arrested person before a magistrate runs from the moment of actual detention or only from the time police formally record the arrest.
cases.bench: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar
cases.status_text: 24 hours run from detention; bail granted
cases.last_event: The Court held that the 24-hour deadline runs from actual detention and that "any attempt to draw an artificial distinction between detention and arrest is constitutionally unsustainable." Only the time needed for the journey to the magistrate can be excluded. The four men had been detained at 2 pm on 29 Sep 2025 but shown as arrested at 11 am the next day. The bench set aside the Tripura High Court's judgment and ordered their release on bail, and said magistrates must record when liberty was actually curtailed and may refuse remand under Section 58 of the BNSS if custody is unreasonable.
cases.next_step: Bail conditions to be set by the Special Court. The ruling applies to magistrates across the country.

cases.case: Tarun J. Tejpal v. State of Goa (criminal appeal against conviction, with plea to suspend sentence)
cases.issue: Whether the Bombay High Court at Goa was right to overturn Tarun Tejpal's 2021 acquittal and sentence him on 6 Aug 2026 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment for raping a junior colleague in a Goa hotel lift in November 2013, and whether the sentence should be suspended while the appeal is heard.
cases.bench: Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale
cases.status_text: Suspension of sentence refused; appeal pending
cases.last_event: After hearing senior advocate Kapil Sibal for Tejpal and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for Goa, the bench said it was "not inclined to suspend the sentence", so the 10-year term stays in force while the appeal is pending.
cases.next_step: Hearing of the appeal against conviction; no date reported. Goa has separately sought a higher sentence of life imprisonment (reported).

cases.case: Union of India's applications to modify the Supreme Court's OBC creamy layer judgment of 11 Mar 2026 (appeals from the Madras, Delhi and Kerala High Courts)
cases.issue: Whether the salary income of parents employed in public sector undertakings can be counted mechanically to place OBC civil services candidates in the creamy layer, under the 1993 Office Memorandum and the 2004 clarificatory letter.
cases.bench: Justices P.S. Narasimha and R. Mahadevan
cases.status_text: Centre's plea to modify rejected; two more months to comply
cases.last_event: The bench refused to modify its 11 Mar 2026 judgment, said its interpretation is binding under Article 141 and that parents' salary cannot be mechanically included, ruled that the creamy layer principle as interpreted will govern service allocation for OBC candidates of the Civil Services Examination 2025, declined to set the two-year timeline the Centre sought for PSU and bank post equivalence, extended the time to comply by two months and disposed of the applications. Completed selections, appointments and allocations are not reopened.
cases.next_step: Centre to comply within the extended two months; similar pending cases before courts and tribunals to be decided on the March interpretation.

cases.case: In Re: Policy Strategy for Grant of Bail (suo motu), Uttar Pradesh under-trials
cases.issue: Under-trial prisoners in Uttar Pradesh who have been granted bail but remain in custody because they cannot furnish sureties or meet other bail conditions.
cases.bench: Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale
cases.status_text: Release directions extended to all 75 districts
cases.last_event: Uttar Pradesh told the bench that in 20 districts it found 264 under-trials with bail still in custody, 158 since released and decisions pending for 106. The bench extended the exercise to all 75 districts, said 'the onus lies on the state' to secure their release, directed the state to work with District Legal Services Authorities for all such prisoners, including those with private counsel, and asked trial courts to modify bail conditions where necessary.
cases.next_step: Next hearing 20 Jan 2027.

cases.case: State of Himachal Pradesh v. State of Punjab and others (BBMB share arrears, suit filed in 1996)
cases.issue: How Punjab and Haryana should pay Himachal Pradesh arrears of its 7.19% share in Bhakra Beas Management Board projects, fixed by the Supreme Court in September 2011 and payable from November 1966 for Bhakra and from the late 1970s for Dehar and Pong.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana
cases.status_text: Arrears to be paid in power: 11,973 million units over 20 years
cases.last_event: The bench approved a cashless settlement under which Punjab and Haryana will supply Himachal 11,973 million units of BBMB power over 20 years (Punjab had sought 30 years, Himachal 10, the Attorney General proposed 15). Punjab's objections were not accepted. Himachal's Advocate General Anup Kumar Rattan announced the outcome in Shimla on 6 Nov 2026 and put the gain at ₹600 crore to ₹800 crore a year.
cases.next_step: Supply schedule to run over 20 years, drawn between October and March according to the state. Himachal says it will pursue water cess and the return of the Shanan project separately.

cases.case: In Re: post on the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee's X handle about CJI Surya Kant (suo motu criminal contempt, from letters of advocates Vineet Jindal and Sreejesh SR)
cases.issue: Whether an October 12, 2026, post on the Congress Kerala X handle telling CJI Surya Kant to 'resign now' amounts to criminal contempt.
cases.bench: Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi
cases.status_text: Show-cause notice to KPCC office-bearers
cases.last_event: The bench issued a show-cause notice to all KPCC office-bearers, exempted them from personal appearance, asked the Attorney General to assist and indicated that senior advocate Arvind Datar and advocate Siddharth Agarwal would be amici curiae. Counsel said an 'unconditional and unqualified apology would be tendered'. The bench said any attempt to undermine the court must be dealt with 'an iron hand'.
cases.next_step: Office-bearers to reply to the notice; no next date reported.
